messages.subject: Point count effort area change?
parts:
Is there anyway to account for part of a point count's radius not being included in a survey? In some bird point counts that I did near a river some erosion took place and land disappeared into swift moving water. On one hand this is just part of the early successional riparian habitat that we were surveying, on another hand because we were only counting birds that were not mid air and were using the habitat that slice of the point no longer could have any birds in it. 

I think in a similar example with transect counts where part of the transects was to foggy to count a solution of reducing the transect length was suggested so I was wondering if there was an equivalent for point counts.

It might not matter to much but I was just trying to be through as this is a for my dissertation and it wasn't something we anticipated to happen but events like this aren't predictable.

Stephanie

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Point count effort area change?
parts:
Stephanie

Yes, the consequence of this is likely to be small, depending upon the proportion of points near the eroded back, but you can account for this by adjusting the effort for those points as the proportion of the circle sampled.
